title: Aloo Paratha
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, garam masala, amchur, salt

recipe: Knead a soft dough with wheat flour, water and a pinch of salt. Rest 15 minutes.
Mash potatoes and mix with chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, spices and salt for the filling.
Stuff portions of dough with the filling, seal and roll into parathas. Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with white butter, yogurt and pickle.
tips: Classic Punjabi breakfast – hearty and filling.
Generous ghee and a dollop of white butter make it authentic.

title: Chole Bhature
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, chole masala, tea bag (for colour)

recipe: Pressure-cook chickpeas with a tea bag for dark colour. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with chole masala and simmer the chickpeas in it.
Knead maida with yogurt, a little oil and water into a soft dough. Rest, roll into discs and deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Serve hot bhature with chole, onion rings and pickle.
tips: Iconic Amritsari / Punjabi weekend breakfast or brunch.
Fluffy bhature and well-spiced chole are the hallmark.

title: Amritsari Aloo Kulcha
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, nigella seeds, spices

recipe: Knead a soft dough with maida, yogurt, baking powder and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced potato filling with onion, green chilli, coriander and spices. Stuff, roll and cook in a tandoor or on a tawa until crisp and layered.
Brush with butter and serve with chole, onion and chutney.
tips: Amritsar's signature stuffed leavened bread – crisp outside, soft and flavourful inside.
Best eaten fresh from a tandoor.

title: Amritsari Paneer Kulcha
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, nigella seeds, spices

recipe: Knead a soft dough with maida, yogurt, baking powder and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced paneer filling with onion, green chilli, coriander and spices. Stuff, roll and cook in a tandoor or on a tawa until crisp and layered.
Brush with butter and serve with chole, onion and chutney.
tips: Paneer version of Amritsar's signature stuffed kulcha.
Best eaten fresh from a tandoor.

title: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Ginger, garlic, green chilli, onion, ghee, white butter

recipe: Wash and chop greens. Cook with ginger, garlic and green chilli till soft. Mash or blend, thicken with a little maize flour and simmer.
Temper with onion, garlic and ghee. Finish with a generous dollop of white butter.
For roti: Knead makki flour with hot water into a soft dough. Pat into thick rotis and cook on a tawa.
Serve saag hot with makki di roti and more white butter.
tips: The definitive winter comfort food of Punjab.
Slow cooking and white butter are non-negotiable.

title: Dal Makhani
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Whole black urad dal + a little rajma

recipe: Soak and pressure-cook the dals till very soft. Mash lightly.
In a heavy pot melt butter, add ginger-garlic and tomato puree. Cook till oil separates. Add the dals, chilli powder and salt.
Simmer on very low heat for several hours (or overnight on a tandoor/chulha traditionally), stirring and adding cream and more butter.
Finish with a swirl of cream and serve with naan, roti or rice.
tips: The longer and slower it cooks, the better the flavour and creaminess.
Restaurant-style richness comes from butter and cream.

title: Kadhi Pakora
jainNotes: Contains onion, ginger - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Fenugreek seeds, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves, turmeric

recipe: Whisk yogurt with besan, turmeric and water. Cook, stirring, till it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Make onion pakoras and deep-fry. Add them to the kadhi and simmer.
Temper with fenugreek, cumin, dry red chilli and curry leaves in ghee. Pour over.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Thick, tangy Punjabi kadhi with soft pakoras is comfort food.
Slightly sour yogurt gives the best flavour.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
jainNotes: Contains chicken and onion-garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, garam masala (for marinade)
Tomato puree, butter, cream, kasuri methi, honey or sugar

recipe: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices for at least 1 hour. Grill, roast or pan-sear till cooked.
In butter cook tomato puree with spices till thick. Add cream, kasuri methi and a touch of sweetness. Simmer.
Add the cooked chicken and finish with more butter and cream.
Serve with naan or rice.
tips: Originated in Delhi but deeply associated with Punjabi restaurant cuisine.
Mild, creamy and tomato-butter rich – not overly spicy.

title: Tandoori Chicken
jainNotes: Contains chicken and onion-garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chilli, turmeric, garam masala, lemon

recipe: Make deep slits in the chicken. Marinate in the spiced yogurt mixture for several hours or overnight.
Cook in a tandoor, oven or on a grill until charred at the edges and cooked through. Baste with butter or ghee.
Serve with onion rings, lemon wedges and mint chutney.
tips: The smoky tandoor flavour is signature.
Punjab's most famous contribution to global Indian cuisine.

title: Punjabi Samosa
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Boiled potatoes, peas, spices (cumin, coriander, garam masala, amchur)

recipe: Make a stiff dough with maida, oil and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced potato-pea filling. Shape cones from the dough, fill, seal into triangular samosas.
Deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Serve with tamarind and green chutneys.
tips: Punjabi samosas are typically larger and more generously spiced than other regional versions.
Crisp pastry and well-seasoned filling are key.

title: Onion Pakora / Mixed Pakora
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, potato, spinach or mixed vegetables

recipe: Mix besan with spices and water into a thick batter. Add sliced onion or chopped vegetables.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney and tea.
tips: Monsoon and tea-time favourite across Punjab.
Ajwain helps with digestion and adds flavour.

title: Rajma Chawal
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Pressure-cook soaked rajma till soft. Prepare a rich onion-tomato gravy with spices.
Add the cooked rajma and simmer till the gravy thickens and flavours meld. Finish with butter.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Comfort food classic – the longer it simmers, the better.
Often finished with a dollop of butter or cream.

title: Baingan Bharta
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Roast brinjals over open flame or in oven till the skin chars and flesh is soft. Peel and mash.
Temper oil with cumin, sauté onion, ginger-garlic, green chilli and tomato. Add spices.
Mix in the mashed baingan and cook till well blended. Finish with coriander.
Serve with roti or paratha.
tips: Smoky flavour from open-flame roasting is essential.
A rustic Punjabi favourite.
